reason: The wording is right and the entry is right, but the translation YEAR in the source line is wrong, and it is wrong in the way rule 4 exists to catch. The 2 December 1851 entry is not in the 1885 first edition of Ward's translation at all: it is one of the passages she inserted in the second edition of 1888. Proof, from two printings read side by side. (1) IA cu31924027696404, Macmillan and Co. and New York, 1887, one volume, carrying the ORIGINAL preface and not the Preface to the Second Edition, and complete (its entries run on to January 1881). There the text goes straight from the 18th November 1851 entry, ending 'every creature worth loving,' to 'Kindness is the principle of tact, and respect for others the first condition of savoir-vivre,' and then to 1st February 1852. There is no 2d December 1851 entry anywhere in it; its 1851 entries are 16 Feb, 27 Feb, 25 Mar, 6 Apr, 7 Apr, 19 Jun, 2 Sep, 9 Nov, 18 Nov. (2) IA amielsjournaljou01amieiala, the verifier's own scan, Vol. I, New York, The Macmillan Company, 1903, copyright 1893, whose copyright page prints the bibliography 'First Edition (2 Vols. Globe 8vo) 1885. Second Edition (1 Vol. Crown 8vo) 1888. Reprinted 1889 ...'. There the same run reads 18th November 1851, then '2d December 1851.- Let mystery have its place in you ...', then 'Kindness is the principle of tact'. The 1903 text also carries a dozen other 1851 to 1853 entries the 1887 lacks (15 Aug 1851, 7 Sep 1851, 2 Apr 1852, 26 Apr 1852, 6 May 1852, 17 Jun 1852, 27 Sep 1852, 31 Oct 1852, 26 Dec 1852, 6 Jan 1853, 20 Mar 1853, 27 Apr 1853, 14 May 1853, 26 Jul 1853), which is exactly what Ward's Preface to the Second Edition announces: 'In this second edition of the English translation of Amiel's Journal Intime, I have inserted a good many new passages, taken from the last French edition.' So the sentence was first published in English in 1888, not 1885, and a card that prints 1885 makes a confident claim about a book in which the line does not appear. Everything else on the line holds and I could not break it: the scan reads ploughshare and the Gutenberg American text (ebook 8545) reads plowshare and unexpected guests, exactly as the note says; the cut at 'the winds may bring' is at a complete clause and the note discloses the continuation; the entry heading is the opening of the entry; Amiel is not banned and stands at one of three (month 3); shipped.js returns no shipped or near match; no other Amiel in month 5; Diary is the form; the source line leads with the name, carries no em dash and no straight quote, and is 96 characters. Fix the year and it ships.
